chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from Ubaydullah al-Qummi from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Ja'far from his father: 'That Ali (peace be upon him), when he prayed over a deceased person, would recite the Opening of the Book and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).' The hadith is complete.

The explanation in this report is what we previously mentioned regarding taqiyyah (dissimulation/prudence), because we have demonstrated that in the prayer over the deceased, there is no recitation of the Opening of the Book. This report and the one that preceded it are consistent with some of the general Muslims, according to what we previously stated regarding it, so it is not appropriate to act upon it.

key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: The general Muslims (often referring to Sunnis in Shia scholarly context)
key_terms.فَاتِحَةُ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatihah)

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali recite Surah Al-Fatihah during the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) is reported to have recited Surah Al-Fatihah during the funeral prayer (Salat al-Mayyit), a practice noted by scholars as likely being due to *taqiyyah* (prudence) to align with the general Muslim community (Ahl al-Sunnah). Since the definitive Shia ruling holds that there is no recitation in the funeral prayer, this specific report is not acted upon as a binding obligation, illustrating the nuanced application of *taqiyyah* in ritual practice to avoid confusion or conflict with the broader Ummah.
